Ripple Fingerprint
Writeupproject report · ripple-fingerprint 0.1.0

What we built, and what we found

A watermark that a model writes into its own text without changing what it writes. With the key, you can prove which of your models wrote a text, even after editing or mixing. This page walks through the method, the measurements, the demo and the limits.

01Summary

An invisible, provable, edit-robust signature

We built ripple-fingerprint, a Python package that replaces the random draw in a language model's sampling loop with a keyed one. Every token is still an exact sample from the model's own distribution, so the text reads exactly like normal output and nothing can be detected without the key. Whoever holds the key can compute an exact p-value for "this model wrote this text."

On top of the core watermark we added per-model keys from one master secret, so the detector names which model wrote a text and splits mixed documents by source. We made it fast on Apple Silicon (97% of native MLX speed), built a live demo and a results site, ran it across eight local models, and added a page that checks Lean proofs for both correctness and authorship.

02The problem

Proving where a text came from, without making it worse

If you run several models, you want to answer "did one of ours write this, and which one?" for text that has been copied, lightly edited or stitched together. The answer has to come with a real error rate, not a classifier's guess.

We held ourselves to four requirements:

  • No quality cost. The output distribution must be exactly the model's own. Not approximately: exactly.
  • Exact statistics. The false-positive rate you set is the one you get.
  • Local robustness. An edit should only spoil the few tokens around it.
  • Attribution. Tell your own models apart, and never pin one model's text on another.
03The method

Every token is picked by a keyed race

Each candidate token v gets a draw uv, and the token that "arrives first" wins:

next token = argmin over v of  −ln(u_v) / p_v

With fresh random draws this picks v with probability exactly pv (the exponential race, or Gumbel-max trick). The fingerprint only changes where the draws come from: SHAKE-256(HMAC(key, last 3 token ids)). Without the key those draws look like fresh randomness. With it, the detector recomputes them and sees that the winning tokens kept drawing u close to 1.

The detector sums −ln(1 − u) over the text. For text the key didn't write, that sum is exactly Gamma(n, 1), which gives an exact p-value. Because the seed depends only on the last three tokens, an edit only erases the ~4 tokens whose context it touches.

Two details keep the distribution exact across many responses:

  • Repeated-context masking. If a 3-token context repeats inside a response, that step uses ordinary randomness and the detector skips it.
  • Entropy gate. The first ~8 bits of each response use real randomness, so asking the same prompt twice still gives different answers. Without it, generation would be deterministic, and that would give the watermark away.
04Which model wrote it

One master secret, one key per model

Each model's key is HMAC(master, label). The ModelRegistry re-tokenizes a text with every model's own tokenizer and tests it twice per model: on the whole text, and on its best-scoring stretches. Both tests are Bonferroni-corrected across every model and every possible stretch, so the chance of naming any model for text it didn't write stays below fpr.

  • No mix-ups. Under the wrong key, the score is exactly that of ordinary text, even for models that share a tokenizer (Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-0.6B).
  • Mixed documents are split. spans returns character ranges for each model's stretch, with exact edges in our tests.
  • Only your models. It identifies models that sample with these keys. It can't say anything about other companies' models.
05Results

Measured on a confident chat model, the hardest case

Main run: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (MLX, 8-bit), 16 everyday prompts, one fingerprinted and one plain reply each, 300 tokens, temperature 1.0, top-p off. Charts come from docs/make_charts.py.

Other measurements

context_width 2100%100%100%100%
context_width 3 (default)100%100%100%100%
context_width 4100%100%90%70%
  • Quality: mean NLL of watermarked GPT-2 text was 4.02 ± 0.11, against 4.19 ± 0.10 for plain sampling. Within noise.
  • Why chat models are harder: GPT-2 carries about 3 bits of randomness per token; tuned chat models carry 0.35–1.4 (Qwen3-4B: 0.43 mean, 0.07 median).
  • Defaults matter: moving to T=1, top-p=1 and 300 tokens raised detection from 2/4 to 4/4 on Qwen3-VL-4B and from 0/4 to 3/4 on Qwen3-4B-Thinking, with no wrong attributions.
06Engineering

From 71% to 97% of native speed

  • Cheaper race. argmin(E / p) instead of argmin(log E − log p): fewer logs over the vocabulary, and zero-probability tokens still can't win.
  • Precomputed draws. Watermarker.prepare computes a step's keyed exponentials ahead of time; sample() picks the same token either way (tested against the reference formula).
  • Overlap with the GPU. The MLX back end launches the next forward pass asynchronously and hashes the next step's key while the GPU works.
  • Back ends. A NumPy core, a Hugging Face LogitsProcessor / watermark_generate, and an Apple MLX generate that finds LM Studio models automatically.
07Demo, site and Lean

Tools to see it work

  • Live demo (python -m demo.server): generate with the fingerprint on or off with tokens streaming in, tamper with the text, and see which model wrote it, with a token heatmap and a who-wrote-which-part strip. "+ Append" builds mixed documents; "Run every model" produces the eight-model matrix.
  • Sampler visualizer: each token's race animated live, with the top candidates, their probabilities and keyed draws, and the evidence climbing out of the ordinary-text band.
  • Results site: a guided story (site/) from the model card to every chart and reply and the every-model lineup, in light and dark.
  • Algorithmic watermarking: one Lean proof, two questions. Lean checks whether every step follows; the fingerprint names the model that wrote it. The checker runs with a timeout, refuses code that can run programs or define syntax, doesn't count sorry as proved, and can import Mathlib.

08Limits
  • Full rewrites remove it. Paraphrase or translation keeps the meaning but changes the tokens.
  • Predictable text carries little. Code, lists and factual one-liners need more tokens.
  • Greedy decoding (T=0) has nothing to watermark.
  • The key is the whole secret. Whoever has it can detect, forge or strip. Run detection as a service.
  • context_width is a trade-off between edit robustness and repeat-free contexts across responses.
